Sofia / Vanessa — technical notes below that you can pass back to Mariana. TL;DR: BRL cross-border will likely see 1–2 intermediaries; MXN direct collect depends on our legal entity and Mexican banking setup.

BRL (Brazil)
- For inbound BRL from an international sender, most flows use a correspondent in the US/EU and a local acquiring bank in Brazil — expect 1–2 intermediary legs.
- To reduce holds: request sender include CNPJ on the beneficiary field and use the exact beneficiary name; include instruction: "Remittance for invoice 4512 — CNPJ 12.345.678/0001-90".
- Typical intermediary fee band: USD 40–150 (depending on routing and banks). If Globe opts "OUR", ask them to gross-up by an estimate (we can provide a final reconciliation post-settlement).

MXN (Mexico)
- If Globex can pay via domestic MXN rails, they need a CLABE for the MX receiving account — we currently do not maintain a large MXN Nostro in Mexico for the EU entity. Options:
  - Option A: Globex pays MXN to our Redwood Mexico local entity (requires local MXN account and invoice billed to the MX entity).
  - Option B: Pay USD via SWIFT to our USD account and we perform onshore conversion; this route uses correspondent banks and may incur intermediary fees.
- If they insist on MXN to an international account, many Mexican banks will route via an intermediary that charges fees; estimate USD 20–80.

FX and gross-up notes
- If requester chooses OUR (sender-cover): instruct them to add an explicit gross-up line on the payment instruction and optionally include the estimated intermediary fee. We will reconcile and issue a credit or supplemental invoice if the actual fees differ.
- For SEPA/EUR direct transfers, intermediary fees are rare; SEPA should be sent as SCT for zero-cost routing where possible.

Feel free to use the exact language: "Please route as OUR if you wish Redwood to receive the full invoice amount and include an estimated intermediary fee of USD X in the payment details. Redwood will reconcile actual bank charges after settlement."

Happy to jump on a quick call if Globex treasury wants to walk through routing options.
